english: Father, I heard a wolf. Are you afraid? I am afraid. Do not tremble. The dog guards the door. Now lie down and take sleep.
uncertain: ḱléwsoh₂: read as 'I heard' though -oh₂ looks like a present/subjunctive 1sg, not a past

english: Man, how are you living (how are you)? I live, and the gods work goods for me. And how does your lady (wife) live? She lives. May Sky, giver of goods, guard your house.
uncertain: h₁opéyonti: read as 'they work/procure (goods) for me' from h₁op-

english: The old man drives the cow to rest (home). Night came. His own wife milks the cow. Then the old man drove (it in). 'Give fodder to the pig!' Then he gave it food and the pig ate. Then the old man sat down.
uncertain: h₁ésmey 'to him/it' read as the pig
gerh₂ḗn could be 'old woman'? read as 'old man'

english: Give me your dog. I do not give you the dog. He guards my herd. But I will give you two sheep. I do not need(?) the dog. Take wool as payment.
uncertain: ḱwónm̥ ne h₁opéyoh₂: sense unclear, 'I don't work the dog'/'I don't need the dog'; maybe the other speaker

english: Who is Sky? Sky is the father of gods and men. And who is Earth? Earth is the mother. Do the gods die? Men die. The gods do not die.
Mother prepares the food. Father sits. What do we eat? We eat wheat and (spring? fat?). And they eat.
uncertain: nu gʷr̥h₃ónti: 3pl 'they eat' after 1pl question — shift of person?
